 home War Russia struck a market in Zlatopol; 11 people were hospitalised 
 One of the UAVs struck the local market. The attack caused a fire in the market stalls, covering an area of 500 square metres. 
 War 
 Russia struck a market in Zlatopol; 11 people were hospitalised
 Eleven injured people have been admitted to hospital; one woman is in a serious condition.
 by Maxim Krus - 18/11/2026 0 
 URL copy Facebook X Telegram 
 On the morning of 18 November, Russian troops attacked a market in the town of Zlatopil in the Kharkiv region. Twelve people were injured in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy. A fire broke out in the market’s trading pavilions. This was reported by Oleg Synyegubov, head of the Kharkiv Regional State Administration.
 Key points at a glance: 
 Russian troops attacked the market in Zlatopol on the morning of 18 November.
 The number of people injured as a result of the enemy attack has risen to 12.
 Eleven injured people were taken to hospital, including an 11-year-old boy.
 One woman is in a serious condition; stalls are on fire at the market.
 Add UkrMedia to your Google sources 
 Get more of our news in the recommendations. 
 A child is among those injured in Zlatopol
 Initially, the regional military administration reported 11 casualties, but the number subsequently rose to 12.
 Eleven people were injured and taken to hospital. One woman is in a serious condition; the rest of the injured are in a moderate condition.
 Another person suffered an acute stress reaction. Paramedics treated them at the scene of the attack.
 Following the Russian strike, the shopping pavilions caught fire
 A fire broke out at the market following the strike. Rescue workers, paramedics and other emergency services are at the scene. The extent of the damage is being assessed.
 Zlatopil has come under repeated Russian attack over the past week. In particular, on 12 November, an 88-year-old man was killed and two children were injured as a result of shelling of the town.
 Then, on 14 November, Russian troops attacked a local business and the private residential area.
